established: Complete unchanged new-affix selector, level/frequency/weighted picker, existing-group/class-compatibility, item-type/property eligibility and two seed helpers execute against all current affix rows and all18 Valkyrie bases.

Each fixture records the whole ordered eligible pool with weights, exact selected source reference and final seed. Real earlier source-selected prefix groups are excluded. Normal/raw levels1/25/46/99/103/787, magic/rare qualities, both affix kinds three seed states, and forced/unforced attempts are covered.
The complete old weighted picker draws from totalWeight+1, with the endpoint assigned to the last eligible row. Even forced selection consumes the two-way seed draw first.
Raw item level is retained; only affix level clamps1..99. Circlet magic levels multiply each affix frequency by its level. Player supported-property filtering is not applied.
services: Item format100, current base/row/property lookup, current-equivalence item-type classifier and existing item affix storage are declared services. No full source table loader, item creation or property execution is claimed.

The original weighted picker is enclosed in a namespace, and a wrapper records its input pool before delegating. Its body is unchanged. All selected references are pinned extraction row IDs, not assertions about modern binary affix IDs.

Inactive nameless/zero-frequency rows use a valid neutral first-property lookup sentinel to avoid undefined old negative pointer access. They cannot be selected. The modern table parser and invalid-record behavior remain outside this proof.
limits: This is affix selection only. Magic/rare outer orchestration, rare names, property value generation/stat application, item-level side effects, actual NPC inventory/combat/casting/lifecycle/saves and modern/client acceptance remain pending. No learned Valkyrie handler is enabled.

Full legacy CanItemHaveMagicAffix rejects a first socket property independently of the no-sockets summon request. This suspicious old behavior is preserved as bounded supplementary evidence; modern socket-affix eligibility is explicitly uncertain.
No original global item/owner seed allocation or exact modern RNG stream claim. No class completion certificate.
